question: The first Indian meteorological rocket launched in 1963 had a diameter of ______ mm.
solution:
The correct answer is __**75 mm**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• The first Indian meteorological rocket was launched in the year **1963** from **Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS)**, located in Kerala. 
• The diameter of the rocket was **75 mm**, designed for conducting atmospheric studies and weather research. *Hence, the correct answer is 75 mm.* 
• This marked the beginning of India's entry into the field of space research and rocket technology. 
• The rocket used was a **small sounding rocket**, which was lightweight and capable of carrying meteorological instruments. 
• The mission's success demonstrated India's capability to contribute to global meteorological and atmospheric research. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS):** 
• TERLS is located near **Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala**, and was established in **1962**. 
• It was chosen due to its proximity to the **geomagnetic equator**, making it an ideal location for atmospheric and ionospheric studies. 
• The station marked the foundation of **India's space program** under the visionary leadership of **Dr. Vikram Sarabhai**. 
• **Sounding Rockets:** 
• Sounding rockets are suborbital rockets designed to carry scientific instruments into the upper atmosphere. 
• They are primarily used for **meteorological studies, space environment analysis, and atmospheric research**. 
• These rockets provide valuable data on temperature, humidity, and wind patterns at high altitudes. 
• **Milestones in Indian Space Research:** 
• The launch of the 75 mm meteorological rocket in 1963 was a significant milestone in India's space history. 
• India's space program has since evolved, leading to the establishment of the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** in **1969**. 
• ISRO has achieved global recognition with missions like **Chandrayaan, Mangalyaan, and Gaganyaan**. 
• **Importance of Meteorological Rockets:** 
• These rockets play a crucial role in **collecting weather data**, which is vital for forecasting and disaster management. 
• They contribute to understanding **climate change and atmospheric behavior**. 
• Meteorological rockets have paved the way for advancements in satellite-based weather monitoring systems. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Dr. Vikram Sarabhai:** Known as the **Father of the Indian Space Program**, he played a pivotal role in the establishment of TERLS and ISRO. 
• **NASA Collaboration:** The first meteorological rocket launch involved technical collaboration with **NASA**, showcasing early international partnerships in India's space journey. 
• **ISRO’s Evolution:** From launching sounding rockets to developing advanced satellites and interplanetary missions, ISRO has become a global leader in space technology. 
• **Global Impacts:** The data collected from meteorological rockets aids in addressing global challenges like **climate change** and improving **agricultural productivity** through weather prediction.
